s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive renal failure with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Poor appetite and fatigue for a week
Decreased daily urine output to less than 50 mL/d
Laboratory tests showing severe renal impairment and anemia
key_facts: No history of Raynaud phenomenon, swollen fingers, rashes, joint pain, coughing, or wheezing
Urine analysis showing occult blood 3+ and protein 1+

raw.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive renal failure with systemic symptoms

key_facts: No history of Raynaud phenomenon, swollen fingers, rashes, joint pain, coughing, or wheezing

differentials: Proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits
per_call: Proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits

shortlist.label: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with rapidly progressive renal failure and systemic symptoms, consistent with RPGN

shortlist.label: Lupus nephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive ANA, anti-SM, and U1-NRNP, along with low complement levels, suggest lupus nephritis as a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: IgA nephropathy
shortlist.why_kept: IgA deposition in mesangial area on immunofluorescence and electron-dense deposits on electron microscopy are characteristic of IgA nephropathy

shortlist.label: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of rapidly progressive renal failure and systemic symptoms, along with positive anti-SM and U1-NRNP, could suggest anti-GBM disease

shortlist.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation with rapidly progressive renal failure, systemic symptoms, and positive ANA could be consistent with ANCA-associated vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient has a positive ANA, Anti-SM, and U1-NRNP, which are specific autoantibodies associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The presence of low complement levels (C3 and C4) and the kidney biopsy findings of cellular crescents and IgA deposition also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis
rejected.why: While the patient has rapidly progressive renal failure, the presence of specific autoantibodies and low complement levels points more towards an immune-mediated disease like lupus nephritis

rejected.label: IgA nephropathy
rejected.why: Although the biopsy shows IgA deposition, the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings (e.g., positive ANA, Anti-SM, and U1-NRNP) are more consistent with lupus nephritis

rejected.label: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of anti-GBM antibodies, which are characteristic of this disease

rejected.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of ANCA positivity or other typical features of vasculitis, such as granulomatosis or eosinophilia
